JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec. 166 of the M.V. Act through her natural guardian,
seeking SCCH-24 compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident dated 05.12.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 05.12.2020 at about 3.00 p.m., the minor petitioner was a pedestrian along with her aunt Bhavya to go to their home on left side footpath of Magadi Huliyurdurga road, near Bestara Palya, MagadiTaluk, Ramanagar District, at that time the driver of the Honda Jazz car bearing Reg.No.KA41 MB4289 came from opposite side, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against her, as a result she was fell down and sustained grievous injuries, immediately she was rushed to Govt., Hospital, Magadi, and then she was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital,
wherein admitted as an inpatient from 06.12.2020 to 09.12.2020 and underwent surgery and discharged with an advice for follow up treatment.

So far her family has spent more than SCCH-24 Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
3.
The Petitioner further averred that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, was a student.

On account of said accidental injuries, she has lost her classes, education and lost her bright future and she completely bead ridden, she cannot stand, walk, sit and squat on the floor, cannot lift or carry any weight and too difficulty to breath etc.,

The Magadi police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the Honda Jazz car bearing reg.No.KA41MB4289 in Cr.No.263/2020,
offense punishable u/Sec.279, 337 & 338 of IPC.
The Respondent no.1 being the owner, respondent no.2 being the policy holder and respondent no.3 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, are Kumari.

jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her.

SCCH-24 4. In response to the summons, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsels,
but the Respondent No.3 alone has filed written statement.

5. The Respondent No.3 in the written statement has denied the averments of the petition as false,
admitted issuance of policy in favour of the 2nd respondent Sri.Sathyajith R., but their liability if any is subject to its terms and conditions and submitted there is non compliance of Sections 134(c)
and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that there is a 11 days delay in lodging the complaint and the insured car is falsely implicated for the alleged accident to the petitioner even though the insured vehicle was not involved in the alleged accident.

Further submitted that the alleged accident if any was due to the own negligence of the minor petitioner and her guardian by walking on the road in violation of the traffic rules and pedestrian rules.
The driver of the insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the SCCH-24 date of the accident, as such there is a violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by driver of Jazz car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB4289 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, from whom and at what quantum?
3.
What order
or award?
7. The Petitioner in order to prove her case, she has examined her natural guardian/mother Smt.Sowmya as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.13.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N. - Orthopedic Surgeon at Sai Ortho and Dental Center, is examined as PW.2 and produced 2 documents as per Exs.P.14 and P.15.

On the other hand, SCCH-24 Dr.Jnanaprakash S.N.Senior Specialist at Magadi Govt., Hospital, is examined as RW.1 and produced MLC register extract as per Ex.R1.
8.
Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following;
Kumari.

3  REASONS

10. Issue No.1:
The Petitioner, in order prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the car of offending car bearing reg.No.KA41MB4289, examined her guardian i.e., her mother Smt.Sowmy as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1, P2 and P4 to P.7.

SCCH-24 PW.1 has specifically deposed in her evidence that on 05.12.2020 at about 3.00 p.m., her daughter was a pedestrian along with her aunt Bhavya to go to their home on left side footpath of MagadiHuliyurdurga road, near Bestara Palya, MagadiTaluk, Ramanagar District, at that time the driver of the Honda Jazz car bearing Reg.No.KA41 MB4289 came from opposite side, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against her and caused the accident, as a result she was fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

On the other side the Respondent No.3 has contended that alleged accident if any was due to the own negligence of the minor petitioner and her guardian by walking on the road in violation of the traffic rules and pedestrian rules.
But the Respondent No.3 to substantiate this defense has not examined any witness including the eyewitness who had witnessed the accident and also not produced any supporting documents.
In the crossexamination of PW.1 nothing worth is elicited to prove SCCH-24 the defence of the respondent No.3 and to disprove the alleged manner of accident.
Therefore, the defence of the respondent No.3 remained unproved.

11. In support of the defence the respondent No.3 has examined the Senior Specialist at Magadi Government Hospital as RW.1 who has produced the notarized copy of MLC register extract and as per that the petitioner met with RTA caused by the insured Car.
The evidence of RW.1 clearly supports the case of the petitioner and moreover the insurance company has not lead any contrary evidence to this.

12. On the other side, the documents produced by the Petitioner as per Exs.P.1, P2 and P4 to P.7,
such as FIR, FIS, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, MVA report and chargesheet are the public documents which have got presumptive value under law.

The charge sheet filed as per Ex.P.7 clearly discloses that the investigation officer, after detail investigation has filed the charge sheet holding that SCCH-24 the driver of the offending car had driven it in a rash and negligent manner and caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 wound certificate produced by the Petitioner further discloses that, the Petitioner has sustained simple and grievous injuries on account of accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 and the Exs.P.1, P2 and P4 to P.7, this court is of the opinion that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Honda Jazz car bearing Reg.No.KA41MB4289 and same has resulted in simple and grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly issue No.1 held in the affirmative.

13. Issue No.2: It is the further specific case of the Petitioner that as per wound certificate at Ex.P.3, on account of the accident, she has sustained a laceration of 4x2 cm over dorsum of right Kumari.

Sinchana vs Yashaswini R on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32353188/
4 foot with bleeding and right ankle tenderness present with swelling, right foot ankle xray shows fracture of both bones of right leg (lower ends), which is simple and SCCH-24 grievous in nature.
The Petitioner averred that due to this injuries she has became permanently disabled.

The Petitioner in order to substantiate that she is suffering from disability, has examined Dr.Nagara B.N. as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P14 and P15.
14.

The PW.2 has deposed supporting the version of the Petitioner stating that, a patient by name Ms.Sinchana aged 10 years came to him on 13.09.2022 for assessment of disability and she gave an alleged H/o RTA on 05.12.2020 and sustained right leg both fracture of the lower end of the tibia and fibula with lacerated wound over the lower third of the right leg and as per the copy of wound certificate she was initially treated at Govt. Hospital, Magadi and later as per discharged summary,
she was treated at Adichunchanagiri Hospital conservatively with dressing and above knee case and later discharged on 09.12.2020 and she said was on regular follow up in the same Hospital and the wounds healed and the fractures SCCH-24 united and she now complains of pain and weakness in the right leg, unable to sit down, squat and run fast and on examination she has restricted right knee movements and recent xray of the right leg shows united fracture.

The PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner was examined clinically, radiologically and assessment of disability was done and the petitioner is suffering from the permanent physical disability of the right lower limb is at 34% and whole body disability is 11%.

In the crossexamination of PW.2 it is elicited that he has not treated the petitioner, the petitioner took conservative treatment, as the petitioner is young aged person by taking physiotherapy the restrictions of right knee movements will be improved and he has not tallied the old Xray with the recent Xray.

Therefore, considering the evidence, further having regard to the nature of injury, age of the Petitioner, duration of treatment and as the fracture is united, hence the functional disability of the Petitioner is considered as 8% to the whole body.
While discussing issue No.1, this court has already SCCH-24 come to the conclusion that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending Car.
Therefore, the petitioner entitled to get compensation.
Age of the Petitioner 15.
The Petitioner, in order to prove her age, she has produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.9.
As per the said document, her date of birth is 10.02.2012.
The accident was occurred on 05.12.2020.
As such, as on the date of accident the age of the Petitioner is considered as 8 years.
Quantum of Income and quantum of compensation 16.
The Petitioner, as on the date of accident, admittedly was a minor.
Therefore, she was not earning anything.

As per the decision of Hon'ble supreme court reported in ILR 2014 Kar 4891 rendered in Master Mallikarjun Vs Divisional Manager, National Insurance having regard to relevant factors, precedents and approach of various Hon'ble high courts with regard to the SCCH-24 compensation of the child victims, held that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc., should be Rs.1,00,000/
disability up to 10%, if the disability is above 10% and up to 30% to whole body 3 lakhs: up to 60% 4 lakhs: up to 90% 5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be 6 lakhs.

5
suffering from disability to the tune of 8% and she was hospitalized for about 4 days.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ under the head of pain and suffering already undergone including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.

17. The Petitioner was inpatient from 06.12.2020 to 09.12.2020 and has underwent treatment,
obtained follow up treatment.
This must have caused loss of some income and discomforts to the parents of the Petitioner during that period.
Therefore, her parents are entitled for a sum of SCCH-24 Rs.30,000/ under the heads of loss of income and discomforts to the parents.
The guardian of the Petitioner has stated that they have spent considerable amount towards her conveyance and nourishment etc..
Therefore, Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
The PW.1 stated that he has spent more that Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses.
But, in this regard the Petitioner has produced 12 medical bills for Rs.6,213/ as per Ex.P.10.
In the cross examination, PW.1 nothing worth is elicited contrary to the Ex.P.10.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.6,213/ under the heads of medical expenses.
18. Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows: Sl.

HEAD COMPENSATION No.
AMOUNT 1. Pain and suffering already Rs.1,00,000/ undergone and to be suffered in future including loss of comforts amenities on account of disability.
SCCH-24 2. Discomforts, inconvenience and Rs.30,000/ Loss of earnings of the parent during the laid up period.

3. Medical Bills Rs.06,213/
4. Conveyance, attendant and Rs.20,000/ nourishment etc.
TOTAL Rs.1,56,213/
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.1,56,300/ and same is awarded to the petitioner under the above heads along with interest @6% pa..

19. LIABILITY:
The Respondent No.3 has not proved its defence as discussed above.

Therefore, the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are being the owner, policy holder and respondent no.3 is being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.3 - insurer has got primary liability to compensate the Petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.10,00,000/
but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,56,300/ with interest @ SCCH-24 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
Kumari.

6 20.
Issue No.3:

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.1,56,300/ (Rupees One Lakh Fifty Six Thousand and Three Hundred Only) along with interest at 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents 1 to 3 are jointly and SCCH-24 severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.3 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this Judgment.

On deposit of compensation and interest, a sum of Rs.75,000/ shall be deposited in the name of the minor Petitioner in any nationalized or scheduled bank till she attains the age of majority and remaining amount shall be released in the name of the guardian of the Petitioner on proper identification and acknowledgement as per rules.
SCCH-24 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
